subject: BlueHarbor tenant: Conductor plan for initial access & API seeding
messages:
From: Maya Singh <maya@blueharbor.com>

Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 3 Apr 2027 09:11:00 -0700
Subject: Re: BlueHarbor tenant: Conductor plan for initial access & API seeding

Hi David,

Thanks — we’re excited to get started. Short update from our side:
- We have an Okta team ready to provision SAML apps on Wednesday (3/7) morning PST.
- We’ll need two admin users initially (maya.singh, rachel.lee) and a service account for CI.
- Can your team seed API keys into a dev namespace first? We prefer not to use production keys until the smoke test is green.

Attaching a simple matrix that maps roles to people — I added the Okta contact in case you need to sync.

Maya
Onboarding lead, BlueHarbor Labs
Attachments: BlueHarbor_onboarding_MVP_v1.xlsx

Maya — following up with the runbook items we promised on the call.

Summary of next actions (who/what/by when):
- Monica: seed API keys into dev namespace (namespace: blueharbor-dev) and share key IDs — ETA Apr 4 EOD
- Jonas: create admin and service accounts in the tenant project; add role mapping to the shared sheet — ETA Apr 4 noon
- Irene: prepare the minimal tenant-template.json for programmatic provisioning and check required fields for Okta SAML assertion — ETA Apr 3 5pm
- Maya + Okta: share metadata URL and test users (maya.singh, rachel.lee) — ETA Apr 5 morning

I attached the tenant template and the onboarding workbook. Please confirm ownership and flag any compliance blockers (audit logging, key rotation policy).

Attachments: blueharbor-tenant-template.json

Thanks,
David

Redwood Inference
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>

Cc: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 3 Apr 2027 12:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: BlueHarbor tenant: Conductor plan for initial access & API seeding

Hey Maya — quick confirmation from the seed side:
- I’ve created a dev namespace (blueharbor-dev) and generated two API key IDs (kb_9a1 and kb_9a2). Keys are staged in our secrets manager; I’ll share the key IDs in a secure thread once OK.
- For the service account, we prefer a scoped key with read-only telemetry and an admin-level key for provisioning. Recommend rotating after the smoke tests.
- Questions: do you want RBAC roles assigned at project or namespace level? We find project-level simplifies admin invites.

Jonas — can you confirm the initial invite set? I’ll wait to send actual invites until blueharbor confirms the user emails.

Monica
Senior CS Manager
Redwood Inference
Attachments: None

Maya — quick from Jon:
- I’ve drafted the invite list and role mapping in the shared workbook (link: https://drive.redwood.com/BlueHarbor/onboarding-plan). Please add the two admin emails and the CI service account name.
- I’ll trigger invites after Okta metadata is confirmed so we avoid duplicate provisioning.
- If BlueHarbor wants, we can create ephemeral invite links valid for 7 days to reduce manual key exchange.

Small note on audit/logging: Irene and I will ensure audit log forwarding is enabled for the tenant; expect a short checklist on retention settings.

— Jonas
Head of Implementation Operations
Redwood Inference
